topics.title: Agriculture: food security, markets and resource trade-offs
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory sector breadth: connect nutrition, price discovery and farm incentives. Deepen scheme eligibility from official current sources; avoid memorising every old subsidy rate.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: PM-KISAN
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; supplemental income for landholding farmer families.

Family = husband, wife and minor children with cultivable land in State/UT records. Institutional holders and specified higher-status family members excluded; landholding size alone is not the exclusion.
DBT to Aadhaar-seeded accounts; States/UTs identify beneficiaries from land records. Portal, app and remote e-KYC support delivery.
Government income transfer; the cited scheme passage does not specify a Centre-State financing split.

Income smoothing is distinct from a credit subsidy. Land-record targeting can leave cultivators without recorded ownership outside this described route. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; medium/long-term debt for post-harvest infrastructure and community farming assets.
PACS, FPOs, SHGs, farmers, cooperatives, JLGs, agri-entrepreneurs/start-ups and specified sponsored PPP projects appear in the source list; project eligibility still matters.
Participating financial institutions lend; interest subvention and a credit-guarantee route reduce financing frictions.
Government supports interest and guarantee fees; the borrower still has a loan to repay. Loan-facility corpus is not an equal-sized cash grant.

Storage/processing can reduce post-harvest loss, but finance alone does not establish project viability or market access. Source distinguishes financing window from overall scheme duration. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; value-chain gaps, productivity, fisher welfare and employment.
Fishers, fish farmers and workers are the stated welfare focus; pages list infrastructure components, not a complete individual eligibility/exclusion test.
Harbours, cold chain, processing, markets, seed infrastructure, welfare and safety/quality systems; digital registration/benefit-delivery platform is mentioned.
Outlay includes Centre, State and beneficiary contributions. Source lists differentiated Centre-State sharing for centrally sponsored components, not one universal grant rate.

Post-harvest assets connect production to saleable output. Source describes implementation through 2025-26; do not infer continuation beyond that period. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a landholding family includes a member who paid income tax in the last assessment year. Does a small farm guarantee PM-KISAN eligibility?
cards.answer: No under the described source-era rule: family-level income-tax exclusion can override landholding eligibility. Do not test only farm size. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: the only proposed exclusion is that a farmer is a Group D government employee. Automatically reject the family?
cards.answer: No: the cited employee exclusion expressly excepts MTS/Class IV/Group D. Check all other family-level conditions; the exception alone is not a guarantee of eligibility. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: husband and wife both own cultivable plots and have minor children. Two PM-KISAN family entitlements?
cards.answer: Not under the cited family definition: husband, wife and minor children form one family; multiple land titles do not automatically create multiple family entitlements. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: an FPO plans a viable warehouse and asks whether AIF pays off the entire project loan.
cards.answer: No: AIF is debt financing with specified interest/guarantee support, not a universal principal waiver. The FPO remains a borrower and the project must fit eligible infrastructure. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

facts.label: PM-KISAN transfer schedule in the undated scheme notes

observations.value: INR 6,000 per eligible family per year in three INR 2,000 DBT instalments; this is a family amount, not per adult. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: Undated Part 1 p151 scheme design; adjacent p152 separately reports progress as of February 2025, not a current-policy verification date.

facts.label: AIF interest-support limits in the supplied notes

observations.value: 3% annual interest subvention on eligible loan principal up to INR 2 crore for at most 7 years; for a larger loan only the capped portion receives the stated subvention. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: Undated Part 1 pp138-139: financing window described as 2020-21 to 2025-26; overall duration 2020-21 to 2032-33. No claim of present sanction availability.

facts.label: PMMSY period and outlay described in Part 4

observations.value: INR 20,050 crore total outlay including Centre, States and beneficiaries; source describes 2020-21 to 2024-25 implementation extended to 2025-26. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: Undated Part 4 p1, explicitly scoped through 2025-26; no inferred extension to 2026-27 or beyond.

topics.title: Rural credit and microfinance: access with borrower resilience
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Match financing to rural cash flows and compare formal institutions, group finance and borrower-protection risks.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: PM Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY)
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; old-age security for small and marginal farmers; LIC manages the fund.
Source-era entry: age 18-40, cultivable land up to 2 ha in State/UT records as on 1 August 2019. Other pension participation and income-tax/professional exclusions matter.
Voluntary contributory pension; enrolment through CSCs/States, pension after the stipulated retirement age and spouse family-pension provision.
Age-linked farmer contribution matched 1:1 by the Centre; not a non-contributory DBT entitlement.

Small landholding does not override entry-age or pension exclusions. The note's broad government-employee exclusion needs the actual current guideline before adjudication. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: compare an otherwise eligible entrant aged 40 with exactly 2 ha in the specified historical records, and a new entrant aged 41 with 1 ha.
cards.answer: The first is within the source's inclusive age and land ceilings; the second is outside its entry-age band despite the smaller holding. Neither conclusion bypasses other exclusions or the historical land-record date. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a 30-year-old small farmer is already covered by NPS. Is farm size enough for PM-KMY admission?
cards.answer: No in the source-era description: participation in NPS is listed among exclusions. Separate the pension-insurance test from income-transfer eligibility. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

facts.label: PM-KMY source-era entry and pension parameters

observations.value: Entry age 18-40 and landholding up to 2 ha in records as on 1 August 2019; age-linked contribution INR 55-200 monthly, equal Central match, INR 3,000 monthly pension from age 60 and 50% spouse family pension. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: Undated Part 1 pp154-155; land-record reference date explicitly 2019-08-01. Current eligibility and legal exceptions unverified.

topics.title: Banks and RBI: development, inclusion and policy transmission
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Separate financial intermediation from central-bank policy and evaluate whether formal access becomes usable, resilient finance.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)
Finance; affordable accidental-death/disability insurance and deeper insurance access.
Source-era entry ages 18-70, savings bank/post-office account and auto-debit consent; having an account without consent is not sufficient.
Annual renewable accident cover; distinguish permanent total and partial disability from death by any cause.
Subscriber pays an annually auto-debited premium; the cited passage does not establish a fiscal cost-sharing formula.

Risk pooling protects against a specified shock; it is not medical-treatment reimbursement or general life cover. Renewal and account delivery are essential. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
Finance / DFS context; access to basic accounts, remittances, credit, insurance and pensions.
Unbanked persons can open a basic savings account through a branch or Bank Mitra; separate eligibility applies to the overdraft.
No minimum balance; account provides a DBT and financial-services delivery rail. RuPay and eligible overdraft facilities are listed.
Deposit-account infrastructure plus conditional credit/insurance facilities; an overdraft is repayable credit, not a universal cash grant. No fiscal split supplied here.

Account opening is an access input, not proof of active usage or automatic receipt of every linked scheme. The note distinguishes account access from adult OD eligibility. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: an enrolled adult dies of an illness. Is PMSBY the obvious death-by-any-cause cover?
cards.answer: No: PMSBY covers accidental death/disability; the adjacent PMJJBY description is life cover for death due to any reason. Product names and a bank account do not make coverage interchangeable. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a person has an eligible savings account but never consents to PMSBY auto-debit. Does account ownership alone establish the stated eligibility?
cards.answer: No: the source lists auto-debit consent as a separate condition. Do not confuse delivery infrastructure with actual enrolment and renewal. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a 15-year-old asks for both a PMJDY account and its overdraft. Are these the same eligibility decision?
cards.answer: No: the note permits account access above age ten with guardian support but excludes under-18 customers from OD. Account inclusion and access to repayable credit must be tested separately. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

facts.label: PMSBY premium and accident-cover parameters in supplied notes

observations.value: INR 20 annual premium; INR 2 lakh accidental death/permanent total disability and INR 1 lakh permanent partial disability; source lists entry ages 18-70 and annual renewal. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: Undated Part 1 p114 design; the same page separately dates enrolment statistics to 2025-01-15, not the effective date of these policy terms.

topics.title: Health: prevention, access and financial protection
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory syllabus breadth: explain health as well-being and a development input, distinguish prevention from treatment and financial protection from service availability, and prepare one coherent delivery-reform answer.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
Health and Family Welfare; NHA nationally and SHAs in States; financial protection for secondary/tertiary hospitalisation.
Pages describe the SECC-2011/RSBY-linked cohort. For an eligible family there is no family-size or member-age cap in that description; this is not proof of universal eligibility.
Family-floater hospital cover, empanelled providers and day-one cover for pre-existing conditions in the described scheme. Distinct from primary-care HWCs.
Government funded with Centre-State sharing; States can use trust, insurance or mixed implementation models.

Pooling a family limit reduces catastrophic hospital expenditure, but does not make the limit an individual entitlement or establish all later eligibility expansions. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: two members of an eligible family need hospital care. Does each get a separate full PM-JAY annual limit?
cards.answer: No: the cited limit is family-floater, shared across eligible members; use by one reduces the remaining family pool. The source does not multiply the limit by family size. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: an otherwise eligible SECC-linked family has seven members and a pre-existing illness. Reject it solely for these two reasons?
cards.answer: No in the described cohort: no cap on family size/member age and pre-existing conditions covered from enrolment. First establish household eligibility; this is not a blanket statement about all current pathways. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: How can the same PM-JAY benefit operate through a trust or insurer, and why does the distinction matter?
cards.answer: In the trust model the SHA manages payments/claims; in the insurance model government pays a premium and the insurer settles provider claims. Benefit design and purchasing/risk-bearing arrangement are separate policy dimensions. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

facts.label: PM-JAY family-floater limit in the SECC-linked source description

observations.value: INR 5 lakh per eligible family per year for the described secondary/tertiary hospital cover; no family-size/member-age cap and day-one pre-existing-condition coverage in that description. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: Undated Part 1 pp40-41; historical SECC-2011/RSBY-linked cohort described. Later expansions and current entitlement routes not comprehensively established.

topics.title: Employment: people, participation and measurement
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Separate the labour force, workers and unemployed before interpreting a rate. This pilot covers selected concepts, not the entire unemployment chapter.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: MGNREGS / MGNREGA
Rural Development; demand-based rural livelihood security through unskilled manual work.
Rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work; the guarantee unit is the household, not each adult separately.
Job-card and work-demand route through local government; the source describes time-bound work provision, unemployment allowance and Gram Sabha social audit.
Source separates Central financing of unskilled wages from shared material/skilled costs; this is public wage employment, not an insurance premium.

Work demand → employment/income support → potential community assets. Delayed provision/payment or weak social audit can weaken protection. Do not use the note's wage-law sentence as a current legal rule. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
e-Shram portal
Labour and Employment; national database of unorganised workers and support for welfare-scheme delivery.
Source explicitly includes migrant, construction, gig and platform workers; it does not supply a complete enrolment eligibility/exclusion rule.
Records identity, occupation, address, education, skills and family details to support employability and welfare delivery.
Administrative database/delivery infrastructure; no automatic cash benefit or funding split is specified on this page.

Identification can reduce fragmentation, but registration is not itself proof that a worker qualifies for every linked social-security scheme. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: two adult members of one rural household volunteer for work. Does the source promise a separate annual guarantee to each?
cards.answer: No: the described guarantee is 100 days per rural household per financial year, not 100 per adult. Household-level protection differs from counting individual workers employed. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Trace the employment-guarantee mechanism and identify an implementation bottleneck.
cards.answer: Documented demand should trigger time-bound employment; failure is linked in the note to unemployment allowance. Gram Sabha social audit provides accountability. Demand not recorded or delayed provision can break the protection chain. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a migrant platform worker registers on e-Shram and assumes every welfare payment is now assured. What is the error?
cards.answer: The database explicitly includes such worker categories, but registration supports identification/delivery; it does not prove eligibility for every underlying benefit. The cited page supplies no universal payment promise. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

facts.label: MGNREGA household guarantee and response period in supplied notes

observations.value: 100 days per financial year per rural household volunteering adult labour; employment within 15 days of demand, failing which the note describes unemployment allowance. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: Undated Part 2 p43 source-era statutory description; applicability, wage notification and operational/legal exceptions need current verification.

topics.title: Poverty: incidence, depth, capabilities and vulnerability
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: distinguish absolute, relative and multidimensional poverty; interpret incidence versus shortfall, trace poverty traps and match persistent deprivation or temporary shocks to suitable policy responses.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: DAY-NRLM
Rural Development, implemented with SRLMs; rural poverty reduction through women-led institutions and sustainable livelihoods.
Rural poor households, especially women organised into SHGs and federations; revolving-fund access depends on group maturity and disciplined practices.
Savings, internal lending, bank linkage, community investment and livelihood support; Panchasutra includes meetings, savings, lending, repayment and bookkeeping.
Source lists differentiated Centre-State shares, partial World Bank support, revolving funds and federation on-lending; not all support is an individual grant.

Collective organisation → financial access/capability → livelihood investment. Credit can help, but poor enterprise returns or repayment stress can constrain poverty reduction. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Why are DAY-NRLM and MGNREGA complements rather than interchangeable poverty programmes?
cards.answer: NRLM builds women-led groups, savings, credit and livelihoods; MGNREGA offers demand-based unskilled wage employment. Institutional/enterprise capability and short-run wage-income protection address different constraints. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a newly named SHG with no meetings or books claims immediate NRLM revolving-fund eligibility. Does the label suffice?
cards.answer: No: the source ties revolving-fund support to group maturity and Panchasutra discipline. Meetings, savings, internal lending, repayments and bookkeeping are mechanisms for credible collective finance, not decorative conditions. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

topics.title: Education: access, learning and equitable opportunity
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory syllabus breadth: distinguish forms of learning, enrolment and meaningful educational opportunity; explain access–quality–equity and prepare a reform answer that separates policy aspirations from achieved results.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: Samagra Shiksha 2.0
Education; integrated pre-primary to Class XII support, RTE implementation, equity, teacher training and foundational learning.
Government/aided-school system across stages; cited pages emphasise social/gender gaps, disability inclusion and disadvantaged communities rather than an individual cash-eligibility test.
School infrastructure, educational materials, teacher/vocational support and targeted hostel provision alongside FLN goals.
Source states total and Central outlay for the 2021-22 to 2025-26 phase; it is programme finance, not a uniform per-child grant.

Access inputs and attendance must translate into learning; assess teacher capability and foundational outcomes, not enrolment alone. Scope is the stated programme phase. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
PM POSHAN
Education; school nutrition with attendance, retention and community-participation objectives.
Balvatika and Classes I-VIII in the covered government/government-aided and other school categories described; not every child in every school automatically qualifies.
One hot cooked school-day meal; pages connect nutrition with schooling rather than an unconditional household income transfer.
Centrally sponsored; source gives material-cost norms scoped to 2024-25 and permits additional State/UT spending, not a total-meal-cost figure.

Nutrition can support attendance and learning readiness. Page 104's claim that PM POSHAN merges ICDS is doubtful and is deliberately NOT adopted. Stated phase ends 2025-26. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: A school system expands buildings and enrolment. Why is that insufficient to establish Samagra Shiksha's development objective?
cards.answer: The scheme also targets foundational learning, teacher capability, inclusion and social/gender gaps. Inputs/access must translate into competencies; enrolment alone does not establish learning or equitable quality. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a child in a covered government primary school and a child in an ordinary private unaided school both claim automatic PM POSHAN coverage. What can this passage establish?
cards.answer: The first fits the stated school/class route subject to actual programme conditions. The second is not established by the listed covered categories. School type and education stage matter; do not infer universal child coverage. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

facts.label: PM POSHAN material-cost norms labelled 2024-25 in supplied notes

observations.value: Per child per school day material-cost figures: INR 6.78 Balvatika/primary and INR 10.17 upper primary; these are source-labelled material norms, not total meal costs or certified present rates. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
observations.as_of: 2024-25 norms as labelled in undated Part 1 p105; later revisions not verified.

topics.title: Gender: agency, resources, care and participation
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: use health, education, work and representation as distinct lenses; explain how norms, unpaid care and asset control shape agency, then evaluate an equity-oriented policy mix without relying on one headline ratio.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)
Women and Child Development nodal, with Health and Education; girl-child survival, protection, education and participation.
Parents/couples, adolescents, health providers, frontline workers and community institutions are intervention audiences; the passage does not promise a per-girl payment.
Advocacy, multi-sector district convergence and enforcement against sex selection; coordinated task forces oversee implementation.
No benefit amount or funding split established by the BBBP passage on these pages; do not borrow the preceding scheme's funding sentence.

Changing social norms requires service access and enforcement, not publicity alone. Historical district expansion counts in the note are not certified current coverage. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a family hears the BBBP name and expects a fixed cash payment for each daughter. Can these pages establish that claim?
cards.answer: No. They describe awareness, departmental convergence, sex-selection prevention and education/participation goals, not a fixed per-girl payment. Do not infer a cash entitlement from an empowerment objective. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: How could women-led SHGs improve agency as well as financial access?
cards.answer: Regular collective meetings, own savings, internal lending and federation support can strengthen participation and livelihood capability. This is a reasoned policy mechanism, not proof that membership automatically improves every woman's bargaining power. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

topics.title: Urbanisation and migration: drivers, agglomeration and inclusion
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: distinguish urban population growth from migration alone, explain push–pull drivers and agglomeration, assess origin/destination effects and match urban-service and inclusion policies to real constraints.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: PMAY-U: older scheme description (not PMAY-U 2.0 rules)
Housing and Urban Affairs; pucca housing for eligible urban households including slum dwellers.
Source defines the beneficiary family and a no-pucca-house-anywhere condition; an adult earning member may be separate in this older description.
Older ISSR, CLSS, AHP and BLC routes; ARHCs are mentioned for urban migrants/poor.
The note lists component-specific central assistance and a generic sharing paragraph; their interaction is not resolved here, so no universal funding ratio is taught.

Housing ownership, rental access and loan subsidy tackle different constraints. Do NOT transfer old CLSS/MIG slabs, family rules or subsidy amounts to PMAY-U 2.0. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
PMAY-U 2.0: version identification only
Housing and Urban Affairs; the visually read ministry mindmap links PMAY-U (2015) to PMAY-U 2.0 (2024).
Eligibility, income bands and exclusions are not supplied by the cited mindmap.
No benefit amounts, verticals or implementation conditions can be established from this version label.
Funding design not established by this page; older PMAY-U funding cannot be silently reused.

Evidence gap is substantive: this source establishes a version label/year, not the current operational guideline. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a borrower applies an older PMAY-U CLSS subsidy slab to PMAY-U 2.0 because the names are similar. Is the inference supported?
cards.answer: No. Part 2 describes older ISSR/CLSS/AHP/BLC; the visually read mindmap separately labels PMAY-U 2.0 as 2024. That label does not establish 2.0 income bands, benefits, verticals or eligibility. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Why might housing ownership assistance alone miss an urban migrant's immediate housing constraint?
cards.answer: A mobile worker may need affordable rental access rather than a purchase loan or an owned house. The source explicitly mentions ARHCs for urban migrants and poor; this does not establish any individual's current rental eligibility. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

topics.title: Sustainability: resource limits, policy and intergenerational equity
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: connect present needs with future resource availability, explain growth–environment mechanisms, evaluate policy instruments and SDG implementation without treating an income threshold as automatic environmental repair.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: AMRUT 2.0
Housing and Urban Affairs; urban water security, water supply, sewerage/septage and circular water management.
Water-supply objective covers urban local bodies broadly; sewerage/septage objective is separately scoped to the 500 AMRUT cities in the note.
City Water Balance/Action Plans feed State plans; reuse, aquifer/water-body restoration and service monitoring complement physical connections.
Centre, States and ULBs finance projects; source links releases/outcome-based funding to approved plans and outcomes.

Connections alone do not secure water: reduce non-revenue water, maintain assets, reuse treated water and build financially capable ULBs. Stated mission phase: 2021-22 to 2025-26. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a small ULB outside the 500 AMRUT-city sewerage group expects identical water and sewerage coverage commitments. Is the scope identical in the source?
cards.answer: No. The water-supply objective is broadly across ULBs, while universal sewerage/septage is separately scoped to 500 AMRUT cities. Read the service-specific denominator before comparing coverage. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Trace a water-security mechanism beyond installing more taps.
cards.answer: City water balances identify demand/supply gaps; reuse of treated wastewater, water-body/aquifer restoration and lower non-revenue water reduce pressure on freshwater. ULB finances and maintenance constrain the durability of service gains. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

topics.title: Positive discrimination: substantive equality and representation
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory syllabus breadth: explain why identical treatment can preserve historical disadvantage, distinguish reservation from wider inclusion and evaluate representation, targeting and complementary capability support without asserting unverified legal details.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan / accessibility framework
Social Justice and Empowerment / DEPwD; barrier-free built environment, transport and ICT for persons with disabilities.
Accessibility removes environmental barriers to participation; the cited campaign description is not an individual cash-transfer eligibility test.
Audits, retrofitting, accessible transport/websites and crowdsourced issue reporting through the Sugamya Bharat App.
Retrofitting allocations are mentioned; the cited passage does not establish a complete current funding formula.

Formal entitlement without physical/digital accessibility may not create real opportunity. Page 5 describes absorption into SIPDA's barrier-free-environment component; current institutional status remains unverified. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Original illustrative mini-case: a public service is legally available but its office has stairs and its website cannot be used with assistive technology. Is formal equality enough?
cards.answer: No: Sugamya's built-environment, transport and ICT pillars target barriers between formal access and real participation. The case illustrates substantive opportunity, not a newly created cash benefit. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

topics.title: Growth and development: output, distribution and transformation
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: distinguish real output expansion from inclusive development; explain productivity and structural change, then test jobs, capabilities and environmental costs rather than dumping GDP figures.

tables.title: Scheme design: beneficiaries, delivery and source-era limits

cells: UMANG
Electronics and IT / NeGD; unified access to Central/State government services.
Citizen service users; access to the application does not remove each underlying scheme's eligibility conditions.
Multi-platform service aggregation; the cited July 2021 map integration describes locating facilities, including Mera Ration fair-price-shop navigation.
Platform/service delivery, not a separate universal transfer; funding split not established by the cited pages.

Lower search/transaction costs can improve access. Finding a ration shop is NOT evidence that ONORC portability eligibility or authentication rules are met. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Can the cited UMANG/Mera Ration facility-locator description establish ONORC food-portability rules?
cards.answer: No. Locating a fair-price shop is a service-discovery function. These pages do not establish ONORC eligibility, ration entitlements, authentication, portability coverage or the migrant split-with-family mechanism; those remain an evidence gap. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.

cards.question: Why can fisheries cold chains and markets matter for development even if production already rises?
cards.answer: The PMMSY components address post-harvest quality, transport, market access and worker welfare, connecting output to usable income and jobs. More production without downstream capacity can leave value-chain constraints unresolved. Source-era only; verify current guideline. topics.title: Human development: capabilities, human capital and feedback
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: explain real freedoms as the end of development, human capital as a productive means, the growth–capability feedback loop and why average index gains can hide exclusion.

cards.question: Build a short descriptive answer linking health protection, school meals and accessibility to human development.
cards.answer: Hospital financial protection can reduce impoverishing medical shocks; school nutrition supports attendance/readiness; accessible buildings/transport/ICT enable participation. These are complementary capability channels, not a claim that spending automatically produces outcomes. Source-era only; verify current guideline. Operational status uncertain; undated notes are not current certification.
